claim: Let \(1<q<2\) and \(0<\omega<1\). On \(\mathbb R^2\), let \(d^{(2)}(\omega,q)\) have norm \(\|(x_1,x_2)\|_{\omega,q}=((x_1^*)^q+\omega(x_2^*)^q)^{1/q}\), where \(x_1^*\ge x_2^*\ge0\) is the nonincreasing rearrangement of \((|x_1|,|x_2|)\). Put \(t=\omega^{2/(2-q)}\). Then \[d_{\mathrm{BM}}(d^{(2)}(\omega,q),\ell_2^2)^2=\begin{cases}\displaystyle \frac{2(1+t)^{(2-q)/q}}{(1+\omega)^{2/q}},&0<\omega\le 2^{q/2}-1,\\[6pt]\displaystyle (1+t)^{(2-q)/q},&2^{q/2}-1\le\omega<1.\end{cases}\] An optimal Euclidean pullback norm is the ordinary Euclidean norm up to a positive scalar factor. The phase boundary \(\omega=2^{q/2}-1\) is exactly where the Euclidean radial values of the Lorentz norm at an axis and at a diagonal coincide.
integrity: The proof is analytic, treats arbitrary linear isomorphisms through quadratic-form symmetrization, and does not infer an infinite statement from finite computation.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is restricted to real two-dimensional Lorentz spaces with exponent strictly between one and two and weight strictly between zero and one. Literature inspection found no exact Banach–Mazur formula in the checked sources, but a differently notated prior calculation remains a residual search risk.
title: Exact Euclidean Banach–Mazur distance for two-dimensional Lorentz spaces below exponent two
